correctness.rationale: The theorem has an exact finite domain {6,7,8}. For every n its bundled geodesics.json lists exactly F_n vertex sequences; standard-library verify.py builds every valid vertex and every graph edge (38/71/130), tests every step, computes actual graph distances by independent BFS, and confirms edge coverage (38/71/130). Replayed output VERIFICATION_OK. The all-n lower bound uses the F_n first-coordinate edges and each geodesic crossing that coordinate at most once. Isometry is proved by deleting unwanted ones then adding desired ones. The same certificates force gp_e<=2F_n, while first and last coordinate edge classes give >=2F_n. No extrapolation outside the finite domain.

value.rationale: This is not a random small graph census: it directly resolves three successive previously open dimensions of an explicit 2023 published conjecture, with each upper bound independently supported by a minimal exact shortest-path *covering* certificate. The latter settles a natural separate graph invariant in these dimensions and provides concrete, verifiable combinatorial objects for methods attempting the open infinite conjecture. The 42 short paths together cover 239 distinct edges; obtaining sharp covers is not a direct formula substitution from the published lower bound. Its relevance is finite and precise; no unsupported general theorem is claimed.
